items.stem: An LLC with two members elects to be taxed as an S corporation. How is ordinary business income generally taxed?

options.text: At the entity level at corporate rates
options.rationale: S corporations are generally pass-through; they do not pay corporate income tax on ordinary income.

options.text: Passed through to shareholders and taxed on their individual returns
options.rationale: Correct: S-corporation ordinary income passes through to shareholders in proportion to stock ownership and is taxed on their 1040s.
Pass-through income is taxed when earned, not when distributed.
The income is taxable to the shareholders.

items.explanation: Correct: S-corporation ordinary income passes through to shareholders in proportion to stock ownership and is taxed on their 1040s.

items.stem: A business buys qualifying equipment and wants the largest first-year write-off. Which provision allows immediate expensing up to an annual limit?

options.rationale: Correct: Section 179 lets a business elect to expense qualifying property immediately, subject to annual dollar and income limits.
Straight-line spreads the cost evenly over the recovery period.
Amortization applies to intangibles, not equipment.

items.explanation: Correct: Section 179 lets a business elect to expense qualifying property immediately, subject to annual dollar and income limits.

items.stem: Which TWO are separately stated items that pass through to partners rather than being included in ordinary business income? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: charitable contributions are separately stated so partners apply their own limits.
Correct: Section 1231 gains and losses are separately stated for character at the partner level.
COGS is part of ordinary business income.
Wages are an ordinary deduction, not separately stated.
Ordinary business rent is part of ordinary income.
